questions.s: In SQL, the wildcard % in a LIKE pattern stands for:
o: Exactly one character at that place
Only digits from zero to nine
A single space between two words
Any number of characters, including none
questions.e: % matches a string of any length. The underscore _ is the one that matches exactly one character.

questions.s: Which of the following is an aggregate function in SQL?
questions.e: Aggregate functions such as SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX and COUNT return a single value for a set of rows. WHERE and JOIN are clauses.

questions.s: A foreign key is used to:
o: Encrypt all the data in the table
Sort the records into alphabetical order
Link a column to the primary key of another table
Delete the duplicate copies of tables
questions.e: A foreign key holds values that must exist as the primary key in the related table, which enforces the relationship between the tables.

questions.s: Which constraint ensures that a column cannot contain empty (NULL) values?
questions.e: NOT NULL forces every record to have a value. UNIQUE prevents duplicates but, depending on the system, may still allow NULL.

questions.s: Which of the following describes a one-to-many relationship?
o: One student has exactly one roll number
One teacher teaches many students in a class
Many students use many books in a library
One country has exactly one capital city
questions.e: One record on the "one" side relates to several records on the "many" side. The second option is one-to-one and the third is many-to-many.

questions.s: How is a many-to-many relationship, such as Students and Courses, normally implemented in a relational database?
o: By placing a repeated list of courses in the Student table
By merging both tables into one column
With a third (junction) table holding both keys
By using two primary keys in each table
questions.e: A junction table has a foreign key to each side, turning the many-to-many into two one-to-many relationships. Storing a list in one column breaks 1NF.

questions.s: In an ER diagram, an entity is normally drawn as a:
questions.e: Entities are rectangles, attributes are ovals and relationships are diamonds.

questions.s: In an ER diagram, a relationship between entities is drawn as a:
questions.e: A diamond joins the related entities and is labelled with the verb, such as "enrols". Rectangles represent the entities.

questions.s: What is meant by redundancy in a database?
o: Loss of the database due to power failure
Unnecessary repetition of the same data
Use of too many primary keys
questions.e: Redundancy wastes space and can cause inconsistent copies. Normalisation reduces it.

questions.s: A table is in First Normal Form (1NF) when:
o: It has no foreign keys at all
It contains only one record in total
Every field contains only atomic (single) values
Every field in it holds a number only
questions.e: 1NF requires indivisible values with no repeating groups. A cell such as "Maths, Physics" violates it.

questions.s: A table is in Second Normal Form (2NF) when it is in 1NF and:
o: It has no foreign key in any column
It has no transitive dependency among columns
It contains only a single column in total
It has no partial dependency on a composite key
questions.e: 2NF removes attributes that depend on only part of a composite primary key. Removing transitive dependencies is the extra requirement of 3NF.

questions.s: A table is in Third Normal Form (3NF) when it is in 2NF and:
o: No non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute
Every attribute depends on only part of the key
The table has been given no primary key
All of the attributes of the table are keys
questions.e: 3NF removes transitive dependencies, such as City determining Province when both are stored in a student table.

questions.s: Which of the following is an anomaly caused by poor table design?
questions.e: Insertion, update and deletion anomalies arise when the same fact is stored in many places. Changing it in one record only would leave data inconsistent.

questions.s: What is a candidate key?
o: A column whose value is always NULL
The key chosen only for sorting the rows
A key that points to another database
A column or set of columns that could serve as the primary key
questions.e: Candidate keys are minimal attributes that uniquely identify a record. One of them is chosen as the primary key and the rest are alternate keys.

questions.s: The number of columns (attributes) in a table is called its:
questions.e: Degree counts the attributes and cardinality counts the tuples (rows). A table with 5 columns and 30 rows has degree 5 and cardinality 30.

questions.s: A table has 4 columns and 25 rows. What is its cardinality?
questions.e: Cardinality is the number of rows (tuples). The degree is 4, and 100 is the number of cells.

questions.s: What does the term "data independence" mean?
o: Data can exist without any computer
Changing the storage structure does not force changes to application programs
Each user owns a separate copy of the data
Data never needs to be backed up
questions.e: A database separates logical use from physical storage, so programs keep working even if the storage layout changes.

questions.s: Which person is responsible for the security, backup and performance of a database?
questions.e: The database administrator (DBA) controls access, backups and tuning. End users only use the data.

questions.s: A view in SQL is:
o: A virtual table based on the result of a query
A backup copy of the entire database
A special type of primary key column
A printed report of the table data
questions.e: A view stores a query, not data, and presents its results as if it were a table.

questions.s: Which of the following is a database model?
questions.e: The relational model is the one used by most systems today. Hierarchical and network models are older database models.

questions.s: The set of all permitted values for an attribute is called its:
questions.e: A domain defines the valid values for a column; for example, the Marks domain may be whole numbers from 0 to 100.

questions.s: Which of the following best describes a database schema?
o: The structure or design of the database
The data stored in the tables at one moment
The password used by the administrator
The list of users who are online
questions.e: The schema describes tables, columns and relationships. The data in the tables at a given moment is called an instance.

questions.s: A table has the columns (OrderID, ProductID, ProductName, Quantity) with the key (OrderID, ProductID). ProductName depends only on ProductID. Which normal form is violated?
questions.e: ProductName depends on only part of the composite key, which is a partial dependency, and that is what 2NF forbids. The values are atomic, so 1NF is satisfied.

questions.s: Which statement about a primary key is NOT true?
o: A table can have only one
questions.e: A primary key must have unique values; duplicates are exactly what it prevents.

questions.s: Which SQL keyword removes duplicate rows from a query result?
questions.e: SELECT DISTINCT returns each different value once. The other words are not used for this in SQL.

questions.s: Which of the following is true about the ORDER BY clause?
o: It removes the duplicate rows from the result
It sorts the result in ascending order by default
It deletes the selected rows from the table
It sorts in descending order by default
questions.e: Without ASC or DESC the sort is ascending. DESC must be written for descending order.

questions.s: A transaction that is either fully completed or not done at all follows the property of:
questions.e: Atomicity means all steps of a transaction succeed together or none takes effect, for example a bank transfer. Durability means committed data survives a failure.
For each department SUM adds the non-NULL salaries: IT = 60,000 + 70,000 = 130,000, Sales = 50,000 (Kamran's NULL is ignored), and HR has only a NULL, so its sum is NULL.

o: Zara, Sales; Kamran, Sales; Faisal, IT; Mehwish, NULL
Zara, Sales; Kamran, Sales; Faisal, IT; HR
Zara, Sales; Kamran, Sales; Faisal, IT
questions.e: An inner join keeps only rows with a match in both tables. Mehwish has a NULL DID, so she is dropped, and HR is dropped as well because no employee belongs to it.
A left join keeps every row of Emp, matched or not. There are four employees, each matching at most one department, so there are 4 rows. An inner join would give 3.
Starting from Dept with a left join keeps HR even though it has no employees; COUNT(EID) counts only non-NULL values, so HR shows 0. An inner join would omit HR.
Listing two tables without a join condition gives the Cartesian product: 4 rows × 3 rows = 12 rows.

questions.s: Which of the following is a DBMS software product?
questions.e: MySQL is a database management system. The others are a media player, a PDF reader and a file compressor.

questions.s: Which key in a student table would be the best primary key?
questions.e: A roll number is unique to each student. Names, cities and birth dates can be shared by several students.

questions.s: What is the purpose of an index on a column?
questions.e: An index works like the index of a book, helping the system find rows quickly without scanning the entire table.

questions.s: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the traditional file-processing approach compared with a database?
o: Better sharing of data between users
Centralised security of all the data
questions.e: In separate files, the same data is repeated in many places and copies can disagree. A DBMS reduces this and offers sharing and security.

questions.s: Which SQL statement correctly adds a student to the table Student(RollNo, Name)?
questions.e: The standard form is INSERT INTO table VALUES (...), with text in single quotes. The other forms are not valid SQL.

questions.s: Which statement about NULL in a database is correct?
o: NULL means a missing or unknown value
NULL is the same as the number zero
NULL is the same as a space character
NULL is the same as an empty table
questions.e: NULL marks the absence of a value. Zero and a blank string are actual values.

questions.s: Which type of join returns all rows from the left table even if there is no match in the right table?
questions.e: A left outer join keeps every left row and fills right-side columns with NULL where there is no match. An inner join keeps only matching rows.

questions.s: Which of the following is true about a composite key?
o: It is a key that is used only in views
It is made of two or more columns taken together
It is a key that may hold NULL values
It is a primary key kept in another database
questions.e: A composite key identifies records by a combination of attributes, such as (StudentID, CourseID) in an enrolment table.

questions.s: What does SQL stand for?
questions.e: SQL is the standard language used to define, change and query data in relational databases.

questions.s: What does ER stand for in an ER diagram?
questions.e: An ER diagram shows entities, their attributes and the relationships between them.
MIN gives the smallest value in the column. Two students have 65, but the result is the single value 65.

questions.s: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows before grouping?
questions.e: WHERE chooses the rows that are used. HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY has formed them.

questions.s: Which SQL statement changes the structure of an existing table, for example by adding a column?
questions.e: ALTER TABLE adds, removes or changes columns. UPDATE changes values in rows and is not for structure.
